brief: VIX, VVIX and tech volatility are spiking as yesterday's all-clear rally reverses into a selloff, with VVIX stressed more than VIX and VXN nearing Liberation Day panic levels. The VIX 2/8-month futures ratio, TME's preferred under-the-hood stress gauge, is rising sharply as the market reprices near-term risk above longer-dated volatility, and the short end of the VIX curve is exploding as traders rush into immediate downside hedges. Vanda Research warns the selloff plus the vol spike is reviving CTA selling risk: markets avoided systematic selling on election night, but a break below 27,600 could push CTAs outright short, and a break below 26,800 could collapse CTA exposure toward Liberation Day lows, adding further selling pressure. Against that, skew (via the SDEX index) stays below mid-October levels and implied correlations, while rising, remain far from extreme, so options markets are not yet pricing an outright correlation shock. CNN's Fear & Greed Index is in extreme fear but below October's peak bearishness. TME's conclusion: this is panic, not yet a full Volmageddon, but the risk is that elevated volatility triggers deleveraging that turns the shock worse.
